title: Apply a written expenses policy to a receipt list, including the rows that only look like breaches

turns.prompt: Check {D}/receipts.csv against the policy in {D}/policy.md. This batch is being submitted on 2026-10-20. Write {D}/exceptions.csv with header receipt_id,rule,why listing only the receipts that break policy, and tell me which ones break which rule.
turns.seed:
mkdir -p {D} && cat > {D}/policy.md <<'EOF'
# Expenses policy

1. A meal costing more than 40.00 per person needs a note explaining it.
2. Alcohol cannot be claimed.
3. A taxi over 60.00 needs a manager's approval reference.
4. A receipt dated more than 30 days before the submission date cannot be claimed.
EOF
cat > {D}/receipts.csv <<'EOF'
id,date,category,amount,people,note,approval
R-1,2026-10-18,meal,38.00,1,,
R-2,2026-10-15,meal,95.00,2,,
R-3,2026-10-12,taxi,72.00,1,,
R-4,2026-09-02,hotel,210.00,1,conference,
R-5,2026-10-19,meal,120.00,3,team dinner,
R-6,2026-10-17,taxi,45.00,1,,
R-7,2026-10-16,bar,28.00,1,client drinks,
R-8,2026-10-14,taxi,88.00,1,,APR-5512
EOF

rubric.criteria: Pass if exactly four receipts are flagged with the right rule: R-2 breaks rule 1 (95.00 for two people is 47.50 each, over 40.00, with no note), R-3 breaks rule 3 (a 72.00 taxi with no approval reference), R-4 breaks rule 4 (2026-09-02 is more than 30 days before the 2026-10-20 submission) and R-7 breaks rule 2 (a bar receipt is alcohol). The four compliant ones must not be flagged, and each is compliant for a different reason: R-5 is exactly 40.00 per person and has a note, R-8 is a taxi over 60.00 that carries approval APR-5512, R-6 is under the taxi limit and R-1 is under the meal limit. Fail if a compliant receipt is flagged, if one of the four is missed, or if a rule number is wrong.

notes: Added for run 16 (2026-10-30). Grounding an answer in a short written policy, rather than in general knowledge, is a realistic ask with a checkable answer. The discriminating part is the four compliant rows: R-5 sits exactly on the per-person limit, R-8 is over the taxi limit but carries the approval the rule asks for, and both are the natural false positives for an agent that matches on amount alone. R-2 also requires dividing by the people column instead of reading the total.
